audit_verified_basis: Audit-verified = accepted as faithful by an independent audit of this lineage AND byte-identical in this run (the same ledger entry apart from volatile notes, the same document unit, the same reading-set admission text). The latest audit (20261002T1800Z, 19/20) rejected u0168.s01, which an earlier audit had accepted: its 96 bytes leave the verified list, so the verified bytes are the previous run's minus 96 (asserted by finish.py). The audit named only its rejection, not the 19 units it accepted, so those 19 cannot be added to the verified list from this ledger; the count is conservative. u0168.s01 is rewritten in this run (claimed, not verified, until the next audit).

u0168.s01.repair: The reading set kept a defeasible reading of “Claude should remain firm” whose open exception could make firmness not required, although the source calls the lines absolute and says they should never be crossed regardless of seemingly compelling arguments (u0166.s01) and that the strength of an argument is not sufficient justification for acting against these principles (u0168.s03). Repaired: the defeasible candidate is removed; one strict reading carries the rule as content (completion `unspecified`), chosen from the two cited spans, not silently.

u0062.s01.repair: Its permission rules allowed every operator input classified as specific instructions, a persona or information, including inputs that u0123.s03 says operators cannot give, so VE reported a conflict that the source does not contain. Repaired: each of the three permissions is scoped by the six limits of u0123.s03 as exceptions (the permission does not cover those inputs); no default is added for any other input.

u0123.s02.p1.repair: (1) “Legitimately” made a pure ability reading incomplete: the reading set now keeps three readings, a permission (the word of permission carries it), a conditional permission (legitimacy is a separate condition) and an ability that carries the evaluative as the named open term instruction_is_legitimate. (2) The five permission rules were too broad (a role-play instruction stayed permitted even when it included conduct u0123.s03 prohibits): each is now scoped by the six limits of u0123.s03 as exceptions.

u0166.s04.p4.repair: The permission candidate added a duty on operators and users not to unlock the hard constraints, which the source does not state. Repaired: the permission reading and its two rules are removed; the clause is one checked ability statement (no operator and no user is able to unlock a hard constraint), with no norm and no duty on anyone.

in_the_translation_itself.meaning: The translation has norm and soft-norm units and one fenced clause. A discourse document must record every slot of a unit that has meaning; the translation's reading-set units have unrecorded slots, and the spec (docs/spec/discourse.md 11) says norm and soft-norm composition is not implemented. So the upgrade cannot enter the main document: u0214.s02 stays UNFORMALISED (other:discourse) there, and only the norms-free companion probe is admitted.
